chunks: We said: We have explained in the chapter of the necessity of Imamate, where we indicated to it, that the extension of his hand (peace be upon him) and the fear of his reprimand are not availed by the duty-bound due to what returns to them,
because they forced him to go into hiding by threatening him and did not empower him, so they caused it from themselves.

And that occurred in the manner of someone saying: 'For one who does not attain knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, in his obligation, the ugliness is justified' because what is a grace for him from knowledge did not occur,
so his obligation should be considered ugly.
ai.seo_question: How does the text justify the necessity of the Imamate and the concealment of the Imam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elaborates on the principle of Imamate by attributing the Imam's concealment (ghayba) to the negligence of the mukallafun, who failed to recognize and empower him due to their own spiritual shortcomings. He employs a theological analogy comparing this to a person who fails to attain knowledge of God despite having the capacity, arguing that the resulting lack of divine favor is their own fault rather than a defect in the obligation itself. This reinforces the Shia view that the community bears responsibility for the Imam's hidden state through their failure to fulfill their duty of recognition.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: The answer to this would be that, which we have explained in the context of necessity of Imamate; that his administration of affairs and fear of his reprimand are not availed by the duty-bound due to their own stance, because they forced him to go into hiding by threatening him and did not empower him to run the society.
Therefore, this is an evil that they have caused themselves.

This is similar to a case where someone says, “Religious obligations with respect to a person who does not have knowledge of the existence of Allah, the Exalted, is wrong, since he has not availed the knowledge that is a grace for him. Therefore, committing him to religious obligations is wrong.” In the same way our adversary would answer a question as such – that the infidel did that on his own, because Allah assigned ways to His cognition and gave him the capacity to attain belief, and if he did not respect that and did not attain faith, he did that on his own and this does not render his subjection to religious duties wrong.
